title: Round 101: phosphophyllite and laueite source investigation
scope: Two distinct natural metal-bearing phosphate species, with primary structural/compositional evidence. Identity-only curation; no inferred criticality or microbial process.
status: Curator evidence handoff; independent scientific review required.

selection.name: Phosphophyllite
selection.reason: New Zn-Fe phosphate identity supported by a complete natural-crystal refinement, deposited diffraction table and independent locality-composition study. Natural substitution limits are recoverable from primary evidence.

selection.name: Laueite
selection.reason: New Mn-Fe phosphate identity with a complete original structure and a modern natural composite-crystal study. Explicitly preserves older competing oxidation-state interpretation and deposited model-quality alerts.

exact_receipt.interpretation: Name hits are prior source-discovery query logs and authority inventories, not maintained owners for either selected species. Publication paths and 2025 DOI have no previous accepted experiment owner in the scoped matches.

raw_receipt.scope: Selected phosphate/mineral raw roots referenced by matching record/source/review dossiers; generic inherited full-tree raw inventories excluded.

deduplication.interpretation: No prior maintained owner for either selected mineral in this scoped hidden/ignored/followed search. Phosphophyllite was a broad microbial search lead in rounds 84 and 88. Reddingite is a deferred round98 lead and remains distinct from the existing phosphoferrite owner. Generic authority lists, query logs and related-species mentions do not constitute accepted owners. All 257 all-state issues were searched by candidate names in their snapshot title/body content; no candidate hit. This is not a machine-wide absence claim or a search of every issue comment.

search.coverage: First returned result sets; no pagination; bounded discovery, counterevidence and microbial queries, not exhaustive. Selected primary references were followed.
observed_results: Hill 1977 and Dunn/Norberg 1977 complete official originals; Moore 1965 complete official original.
Grey et al. 2025 DOI 10.1180/mgm.2025.21 complete original and publisher-linked supplements.
Baur 1969 full original preserves competing Mn(III) interpretation; no newly identified formal correction/retraction notice in returned sets.
Phosphophyllite coatings, hydrothermal pigment synthesis and 1992 synthesis are separate abiotic leads, not evidence of a microbial process; full primary experiments not curated in this pass.
Returned laueite Mars nodules paper uses inferred mineral composition and equilibrium modelling; no species-resolved microbial experiment was identified in this bounded search.
Historical phosphophyllite original 1920/1915 publisher metadata discrepancy surfaced; current IMA 1920 accepted, original discovery article not used to assert modern chemistry.

Current IMA secondary reference resolves to Grey et al. 2015 crystallographic Al ordering, DOI 10.1180/minmag.2015.079.2.09. Search and publisher abstracts are leads only; no new numerical Al-ordering claim curated from unavailable full original. Separate approved 2015 laueite-supergroup nomenclature DOI 10.1180/minmag.2015.079.2.02 is a group scheme, not a new laueite species accession.

acquisition_manifest.inspection: PDFs extracted with pymupdf and all primary article pages rendered in contact sheets; all four Grey 2025 supplements read, reports visually inspected; Hill deposited Table 1 presence/structure inspected without re-refinement.

authority.current_edition_check: Official CNMNC homepage, acquired 2026-10-15, links the September 2026 updated list. No assumption based solely on a cached filename.
authority.identifier_policy: Grandfathered years are historical fields, not invented modern IMA approval accessions. No additional external species CURIE is asserted. Specimen numbers and diffraction datasets are not species IDs.
authority.criticality: No criticality claim is made for either host mineral. Elemental Zn, Mn, Fe and P or commodity-list entries do not automatically designate these minerals.

phosphophyllite.accepted_scope: Grandfathered monoclinic Zn-Fe phosphate species, P21/c natural-crystal structure, documented locality-dependent Mn substitution.

hill1977.original: American Mineralogist 62:812-817; all six pages, Tables 2-4 and Figure 1 inspected, with deposited Table 1 in AM-77-046.
hill1977.specimen: One Potosi, Bolivia cleavage fragment, reported volume 5.6e-6 cm3; provenance and full prior chemistry attributed by the author to Hill 1976, not a new bulk assay in 1977.
hill1977.methods: Zr-filtered MoKa single-crystal diffraction at 24 degrees C; 6285 measured reflections, 2482 unique corrected structure factors, 1999 observations selected at I > 2 sigma(I); full matrix refinement including H positions.
hill1977.outcome: P21/c structure refined to reported R 0.032 and weighted R 0.035 for selected reflections. Tetrahedral Zn/P sheets and Fe octahedra distinguish the structure from related zinc phosphates. The earlier model controversy was addressed by 3D data; previous 2D projection was not wholly discarded.
hill1977.limitations: One natural crystal, not all localities or a pure synthetic population. Bond/hydrogen positions have the source-stated X-ray uncertainties. No re-refinement of deposited structure factors was performed.
hill1977.deposit: Twelve-page PDF includes the original article, separator at page 8, deposit title at page 9, observed/calculated structure-factor Table 1 on pages 10-11 and end page 12. This is the same experiment, not an independent replication.

dunn_norberg1977.methods: Partial ARL-SEMQ microprobe analyses of eleven Hagendorf and three Potosi specimens, 15 kV, 150 nA, specified oxide/mineral standards and computer corrections; water measured by Penfield method for one Potosi sample.
dunn_norberg1977.outcome: Hagendorf specimens showed variable Fe/Mn substitution; Potosi specimens had little Mn. Borderline Hagendorf NMNH 814317 Mn:Fe 51:49 is a weight ratio, not atomic occupancy, and the authors explicitly declined a new Mn species given analytical uncertainty.
dunn_norberg1977.limits: Individual analytical table offered on request was not present in the article and was not acquired. Published ranges and the three-analysis Potosi mean cannot be treated as fourteen complete specimen assays. No chemical solubility limit or absence of a Mn analogue throughout nature is inferred.

excluded_claims: Full chemical identity from the erroneous first-description formula
A synthesis or corrosion-coating mechanism based on abstract-only or secondary leads

laueite.accepted_scope: Grandfathered Mn-Fe phosphate identity, P-1 structure, qualified natural laueite/stewartite epitaxy context and preserved specimen/model limitations.

moore1965.original: American Mineralogist 50:1884-1892, all nine pages, Tables 1-3 and Figures 1-4 inspected.
moore1965.specimen: Clear reddish-orange wedge crystal 0.16 x 0.32 x 0.50 mm from Palermo No. 1 Quarry, North Groton, New Hampshire, associated with other secondary phosphates on siderite/ludlamite.
moore1965.methods: 637 visually estimated independent intensities from Weissenberg levels, absorption corrections and least-squares refinement; final reported R 0.122, no observations omitted in final refinement.
moore1965.limits: Hydrogen atoms were not located and OH/water assignments were not directly determined. Hypothetical stewartite/strunzite models and heating of other minerals must not become laueite experiments. Historical strunzite-as-polymorph language is narrowed by later water-content distinction, not repeated as modern identity.

baur1969.original: American Mineralogist 54:1312-1323, all twelve pages, Tables 1-5 and Figures 1-4 inspected.
baur1969.independence: New pseudolaueite diffraction study; laueite bond distances reuse Moore 1965 coordinates and older chemical data. Not an independent laueite assay.
baur1969.counterevidence: Pages 1321-1322 propose appreciable Mn(III) from short/distorted Mn-site bonds while admitting smaller substituents complicate the inference. The current IMA formula remains Mn(II); neither the older hypothesis nor 2025 site calculations directly establish oxidation states for every specimen.

grey2025.original: Mineralogical Magazine 89:234-241, DOI 10.1180/mgm.2025.21; all eight pages, Tables 1-5 and Figures 1-6, plus four supplements acquired and inspected.
grey2025.metadata: Publisher and Crossref confirm authors/title/pages/DOI; online manuscript date March 24, 2025 is not the specimen collection date. Specimen collected in late 1970s at the 84 m level, Hagendorf-Sud mine.
grey2025.methods: Composite rhomb was mixed laueite/stewartite by Gandolfi powder diffraction. Separate peak integration extracted major laueite and minor enclosed stewartite; the minor enclosed component had Rint 0.28 and non-positive displacement parameters, so its refinement was not reported in the article. A separate protruding stewartite blade was also measured and twinning included. Laueite data at 270 K, CuK wavelength 1.54184 A, 1252 independent reflections, Rint 0.149 and 1128 above 3 sigma(I).
grey2025.composition: SEM-EDS metal totals scaled to three: Mn0.66Mg0.17Fe2.17 for laueite, Mn0.92Fe2.08 for stewartite. Table 3 simplified laueite scattering model refines 0.93(2)Mn + 0.07Mg, not the EDS site allocation Mn0.66Mg0.17Fe0.17. Ferric assignment and adjusted OH/water formula derive from bond-valence/charge-balance arguments; no direct oxidation-state or hydrogen assay is presented.
grey2025.observed_epitaxy: Indexed {010}/{100} parallel faces and structure orientation support laueite on stewartite with epitaxy plane {010}; Figures 1, 2 and 4. Stewartite B-1 is an explicitly transformed comparison setting, not a new mineral or the laueite symmetry.
grey2025.hypotheses: Figure 5 is one possible interface protonation/occupancy model; Figure 6 and pages 239-240 suggest heterosite-cluster nucleation and changed cavity solution chemistry. Neither a controlled transformation experiment nor a time-resolved solution assay is reported.
grey2025.supplement1_laueite: Six-page checkCIF report: no supplied structure factors for that check, three A-level alerts (Fe1 and O2 displacement parameters, Fe2 anisotropy), one B-level missing-H/isolated-O alert, nine C and thirteen G alerts; Rint 0.149, goodness of fit 3.36, formula/Z reporting alerts. Empty response placeholders are not resolutions. Some formula/Z alerts reflect reporting/normalization and do not alone prove an incorrect species.
grey2025.supplement2_stewartite: Four-page report has two A alerts about nonstandard B-1 recognition and two B missing-H alerts; the paper explicitly explains the transformed setting. Do not transplant those setting warnings into laueite identity.
grey2025.supplements3_4: Laueite and stewartite CIFs inspected: cell/symmetry, reflection counts, formula metadata and site loops. No H atom coordinates in the listed structural models; generic hydrogen-treatment metadata is not evidence of resolved H positions. No new crystallographic refinement or independent checkCIF run performed.
grey2025.editorial_discrepancies: The article bibliography misprints Moore 1965 terminal water count as 6H2O; original Moore title and current IMA both have 2H2O after six coordinated waters. Page 237 initially references Fig. 3 for indexed faces, whereas the actual indexed-face image is Fig. 4. Curation uses the actual originals/figures, not those apparent citation slips.

excluded_claims: Direct elemental oxidation-state assay from EDS
EDS composition identical to refined occupancy
Experimental proof of proposed cavity chemistry or heterosite nucleation
Microbial activity, extraction yield or industrial deployment

access_and_reuse.raw_policy: Publisher/archive originals, CIFs, extracted text and rendered pages retained outside checkout. Committed dossier contains paraphrased assessment, citations and checksums only.
access_and_reuse.grey2025_license: Publisher explicitly states CC BY 4.0 for the article; supplements linked as associated files. They remain outside checkout in this pass.
access_and_reuse.other_licenses: Free reading access is not assumed to authorize redistribution. Handbook explicitly reserves reproduction rights; older articles have no open redistribution assertion in this dossier.
access_and_reuse.failures_preserved: Initial percent-encoded Cambridge supplementary routes returned HTTP 403; identical public colon-form routes with ordinary browser headers returned the actual PDF/CIF bytes. MSA Baur1969 route returned 403; RRUFF archive succeeded. Guessed CNMNC /master_list returned 404; official homepage and linked September PDF succeeded. RSC 1992 landing returned 403 and its experiment remains deferred.

follow_up: Independent scientific reviews of exact owners and canonical CREATE histories after named validation.

Acquire the full IMA-cited Grey et al. 2015 Al-ordering study (DOI 10.1180/minmag.2015.079.2.09) before adding quantitative Al site-ordering claims; present search/abstract access alone is not used as experimental verification.

Acquire complete Thomas and Weller 1992 phosphophyllite synthesis/thermal paper (DOI 10.1039/JM9920201123) and supporting data before any transformation mechanism; keep it distinct from natural-crystal identity.

Resolve laueite specimen-specific Mn/Fe oxidation state, EDS/refinement site differences, missing hydrogen positions and deposited displacement-parameter alerts with stronger direct measurements or expert re-refinement; do not silently repair source data.
If specimen-level quantitative phosphophyllite observations are needed, obtain Dunn/Norberg individual analyses rather than reconstructing them from ranges/means.
Strunzite, ferrostrunzite and reddingite remain separate candidates needing complete selected originals and contemporary identity review; no draft owners created for them.
